text:
Viktor Arvidsson scored three goals, and the last two came 79 seconds apart late in the third period of a game DET had to wait to put away. The hat trick turned a 2-1 grind into a 4-1 win over CHI. Arvidsson, drafted 112th overall by Nashville in 2014 out of Skelleftea, finished with six shots on goal and a goal on his own 5% look in the second period that tied the game after Connor Bedard's backhand had given CHI the early lead.

The result was less of a surprise than the scoreboard suggested. DET out-attempted CHI 62 to 45 and held a 5.09 to 1.58 edge in expected goals, which measures the quality of chances rather than the count. Our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave DET 91%. The second period was the clearest stretch: DET out-chanced CHI 1.82 to 0.24, and Carter Mazur missed the net on a 29% look. Spencer Knight kept CHI close, saving 1.6 goals more than his 30 shots deserved, while John Gibson faced only 19 shots and made 18 saves.

DET also got a power-play goal from Lucas Raymond, the 4th overall pick in 2020, early in the third. Alex DeBrincat added two assists and Emmitt Finnie assisted on the fourth goal. For CHI, Bedard scored the lone goal but was on the ice for 1.45 expected goals against and only 0.60 for. CHI went 0 for 1 on the power play and took 8 penalty minutes to DET's 2. We'd watch whether CHI can start games as well as it started this one and keep that pace past the opening period.
